en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Chattupāhanavagga 85.
The Training Rule on Vehicles.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs traveled by means of a vehicle.
People criticized, complained, and spread it about:
“How can these bhikkhunīs travel by means of a vehicle, just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures?”
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six travel in a vehicle?"... [as before]...
“Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs travel by vehicle?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs travel by vehicle?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of the faith of those who have it...
And furthermore, monks, let the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: ‘If a bhikkhunī travels by vehicle, she commits an offense of wrong-doing.’"
“Whatever bhikkhunī should travel by means of a vehicle, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Thus was this training rule for bhikkhunīs laid down by the Blessed One.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī was ill; she was unable to go on foot... [and so forth].
They reported this matter to the Blessed One...
[as before] ... "I allow, monks, a vehicle for a sick nun.
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule thus:"
“Whatever nun, not being ill, should travel by means of a vehicle, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Regarding “whatever nun”: whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
A bhikkhunī … [as before] … this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
“Not ill” means:
One who is able is one who can go on foot.
One who is ill is one who cannot go on foot.
"Vehicle" means a litter,
a chariot, a cart, a carriage, a palanquin, or a sedan chair. "One would travel by" means...
If she travels by vehicle even once, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she is not ill, and perceiving herself as not ill, she travels by vehicle, there is an offense of expiation.
If she is not ill, but is uncertain of it, and she travels by vehicle, there is an offense of expiation.
If she is not ill but perceives herself as ill, and travels by vehicle, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she is ill but perceives herself as not ill, there is an offense of wrongdoing (dukkaṭa).
If she is ill but is uncertain [of her state], there is an offense of wrongdoing.
If she is ill and perceives herself as ill, there is no offense.
There is no offense for one who is ill.
In times of distress,
for one who is insane,
and for one who is a first-time offender.
The second training rule is concluded.
